scores.claim_text: Planet operates over 100 satellites (designed, built, launched and operated), including SkySat and Pelican high-resolution satellites and a hyperspectral Tanager satellite, generating a daily-revisit imagery archive of over 3,000 images per point on Earth's landmass.
scores.supports: USPTO patent corpus corroborates an operational satellite-imaging program (72 applications, 28 granted patents pre-cutoff, including 'Multi-Pathway Satellite Communication Systems and Methods', 'Cloud Avoidance', 'Anisotropic Aperture Star Camera', 'Vertically Integrated Backend'). PL is a long-tenured EO operator with public quarterly imagery telemetry; constellation existence is well-established.
scores.M_value: n_total_applications=72, n_granted=28 (well above heuristic-8 threshold of 10)
scores.interpretation: Constellation/operational claim is consistent with patent corpus and prior public disclosure. PL has been operating Doves/SkySats for nearly a decade — this is a baseline established claim, not an aspirational one.

scores.claim_text: December 2025 multi-year low 9-figure ($100M+) commercial Pelican satellite-services agreement with Swedish Armed Forces (SwAF).
scores.supports: Planet's own 8-Ks dated 2026-01-12 and 2026-03-19 explicitly disclose the Swedish Armed Forces agreement (contemporaneous with the December 2025 contract date). SwAF is a foreign sovereign — NOT in USAspending (Heuristic 5: source-jurisdiction limits — foreign-government contracts are off-EDGAR/USAspending and would be UNVERIFIABLE via federal databases). Customer corroboration via counterparty 10-K is impossible because SwAF doesn't file with SEC.
scores.M_value: 7 total hits, 3 on Planet Labs own filings (8-K 2026-01-12, 8-K 2026-03-19, 10-K 2026-03-23). No third-party SEC-filer corroboration available (and not expected, given Sweden is a foreign sovereign).
scores.interpretation: The contract is disclosed in 8-K which is regulator-quality evidence. Caveat: a 'low 9-figure' aggregate over multi-year build-and-operate term is partly contingent on future milestones (satellite services are milestone-billed per Note 7) — this is more of a backlog claim than recognized revenue. Stage-ladder (Heuristic 3): contract is at the SIGNED stage, not OPERATIONAL — Pelican constellation for SwAF is yet to be built and launched.

scores.claim_text: Defense & Intelligence revenue of $180.2M in FY2026 (up from $116.3M FY2025); total revenue $307.7M; two customers at 13% and 12%; one customer 33% of AR.
scores.supports: USAspending confirms PL is a real federal contractor. 'Planet Labs Federal, Inc.' has $57.7M across 16 awards since 2023 (NASA $34.4M, DoD $23.0M, USDA, Commerce). Broader 'Planet Labs' substring shows 31 awards / $77.2M. Federal contracts include named programs: NASA CSDA (Commercial Smallsat/Satellite Data Acquisition), DoD PLANETSCOPE DATA, electro-optical satellite-data imagery subscriptions, regional SAT-EO subscriptions covering ASEAN nations. This places PL squarely in the federal-contract universe (Layer 3 Rule 7 satisfied).
scores.M_value: 31 federal awards / $77.2M total since 2023 (incl. NASA $56.1M, DoD $41.7M when using broader match). Since 2024-01-01: 20 awards / $58.2M.
scores.interpretation: Federal contracts are confirmed but the $180M Defense & Intelligence segment is much larger than the visible US federal contract footprint (~$30-40M annualized). The gap is consistent with: (a) commercial defense (Ukraine $35.9M disclosed, allied governments, NATO members), (b) IC contracts that flow through primes or are partially classified (NGA, NRO), and (c) the FY2026 $180M includes the SwAF agreement and other foreign defense customers. No contradiction — but it's worth noting most defense revenue is OFF-EDGAR and OFF-USAspending.

scores.claim_text: NASA Communications Services Project (CSP) subcontractor: aggregate $40.5M funding, $30.4M received as of Jan 31, 2026; partnered with Telesat and SES.
scores.supports: USAspending confirms PL is in NASA contract universe ($34.4M+ in NASA awards visible to Planet Labs Federal/PBC since 2023, including 'ELECTRO OPTICAL DATA REQUIREMENT' $19.9M, CSDA task orders $13.5M and $6.2M). NASA CSP funding ($40.5M) flows through prime providers, so it appears on the prime's USAspending record, not PL's directly — which is consistent with the filing's explicit subcontractor disclosure. Telesat & SES are public; Telesat (TSAT/TSX) and SES SA are independently identifiable NASA CSP awardees.
scores.M_value: PL has $34.4M of NASA contracts on USAspending (separate from CSP subcontract). CSP funding flows via prime contractors — PL is correctly characterized as subcontractor.
scores.interpretation: Subcontract structure (PL gets paid by prime, not directly by NASA for CSP) is properly disclosed. No contradiction. The $40.5M aggregate vs $30.4M received indicates the program is progressing but not yet complete. CSP is a development/demonstration contract, not commercial-service-live — stage 'demonstration' per Heuristic 3.

scores.claim_text: Patent portfolio covers novel spacecraft features (satellites, imaging, constellation operations).
scores.supports: USPTO ODP confirms 72 applications and 28 granted patents pre-cutoff for Planet Labs PBC. Categories observed include multi-pathway satellite communication systems (multiple grants), cloud avoidance algorithms, anisotropic aperture star camera, and vertically integrated backend systems — directly relevant to satellite EO. Easily clears Heuristic 8 threshold (n_granted >= 10).
scores.M_value: n_granted=28, n_total_applications=72, multiple titles directly matching satellite/imaging/constellation tech
scores.interpretation: Patent claim is fully substantiated. Real, deep technical IP relevant to claimed business.

scores.claim_text: Corporate HQ in San Francisco (~71,280 sq ft) houses all satellite manufacturing/testing/R&D; manufacturing also being expanded in Germany.
scores.supports: EPA FRS would only capture chemical/emissions footprints — satellite assembly is non-emitting clean-room work, so absence in FRS is not a signal here (Heuristic 1 exception). PL's properties disclosure matches its prior filings. Berlin/Germany expansion is reiterated multiple times in this 10-K and prior risk factors. No counterparty-disclosure or registry test is available for a software/clean-room facility.
scores.M_value: Internally consistent in PL's own filings; no third-party check applicable
scores.interpretation: Low-stakes facilities claim. UNVERIFIED is the appropriate label — no contradicting evidence but no positive third-party verification available either.

scores.claim_text: FY2026 net loss $246.9M (net loss balloon vs $123.2M FY25 — driven by $161M non-cash warrant FV change), $1.45B accumulated deficit; positive operating cash flow $134M; $640M cash+ST inv; fresh $460M 0.50% convert due Oct 2030 (issued Sept 2025).
scores.extraction_quote: net losses of $246.9 million... change in fair value of warrant liabilities of $161.4 million... cash provided by Operating activities $134,362.
scores.supports: EDGAR fulltext search for 'going concern' on Planet Labs (CIK 0001836833) 10-Ks returns 0 hits — no auditor going-concern qualifier per Heuristic 10. Net loss $246.9M is HEAVILY non-cash: $161.4M warrant FV change + $55.0M SBC + $41.8M D&A = ~$258M of non-cash items; actual operating cash flow is POSITIVE $134.4M. With $640M liquidity vs $460M of long-dated convertibles maturing 2030, near-term distress risk is low.
scores.interpretation: Reported net loss masks underlying liquidity health — PL has materially de-risked vs prior years. Stock price up 4x in FY2026 (from $56 to $230 indexed) — warrant FV expansion is a direct consequence and a non-cash GAAP artifact. The going-concern signal is negative (no distress signal). PASS.

scores.claim_text: Remaining performance obligations of $852.4M as of Jan 31, 2026; ~34% to be recognized within 12 months, ~65% within 24 months.
scores.supports: RPO is a GAAP-disclosed audited number — auditor-attested per ASC 606. The $852M backlog is substantial relative to $307.7M FY2026 revenue (~2.8x). However: (a) only 34% (~$290M) is expected within 12 months, only modestly above FY2026 actual ($307.7M), implying FLAT near-term growth absent new bookings; (b) the SwAF deal (low 9-figure ~$100M+) is largely milestone-based and back-end-loaded; (c) satellite-services revenue under cost-to-cost has cumulative-catch-up risk if cost estimates change. No SEC-filer counterparty corroboration of $852M backlog is available because key customers are foreign governments/IC.
scores.M_check: edgar_fts.query_fulltext('Planet Labs') across major US-listed counterparties (T, LMT, BA, AMZN)
scores.M_value: 0 hits in any of AT&T, Lockheed Martin, Boeing, Amazon 10-K corpus. 435 total EDGAR mentions, dominated by PL's own filings.
scores.interpretation: RPO is a real GAAP number, but the lack of counterparty corroboration in US-listed defense primes is consistent with PL's customer base being non-US-filer governments (Sweden, NATO, Ukraine, IC). MODERATE rather than PASS because Heuristic 9 (constellation-operational vs announced) applies: a meaningful share of the RPO depends on the SwAF Pelican constellation, which is at the SIGNED-not-OPERATIONAL stage. Stage-ladder execution risk on milestone-based satellite-services revenue is real.
